As a member of the CAD group, you will support the gate-level glitch noise and static timing analysis (STA) methodologies that ensure the signal integrity and robustness of Apple silicon across advanced technology nodes. jobs.title: Frontend CAD Flow Engineer, SI Hardware
jobs.description:
**What to Expect**

The Tesla SI Hardware team is at the forefront of revolutionizing artificial intelligence through cutting-edge hardware innovation. The team designs and develops advanced AI inference and training chips that power the neural networks behind Full Self-Driving (FSD) and Tesla's humanoid robot, Optimus. By creating custom silicon and optimized architectures, the team keeps Tesla at the leading edge of computational efficiency and performance.

Our SI Hardware CAD team builds and maintains the end-to-end infrastructure that takes complex SoC and 3D IC designs from RTL to tapeout. As a Staff CAD Flow Engineer focused on the front end, you will build the flows that RTL and physical design engineers rely on every day: constraints, synthesis, equivalence, static RTL checks, power intent, and the handoff system that ties them together. Building these well takes real technical depth. You will bring each flow up on real blocks, analyze the results until you understand exactly why the tools report what they do, and turn that understanding into a system that gives designers correct, actionable answers. You are not the one fixing every CDC violation, but you understand them well enough to build the flow that helps every designer find and fix their own.

 **What You'll Do**

* Architect and build the RTL-to-PD handoff system: automated quality gates for elaboration, lint, CDC/RDC, SDC, UPF, smoke synthesis, and LEC. Give RTL and PD engineers clear pass/fail criteria they trust
* Build the timing constraint (SDC) flow: constraint linting, block-vs-top and RTL-vs-netlist consistency checks, and templates or generators for common clocking and I/O structures. Produce reports that point designers to the root cause instead of encouraging more exceptions
* Maintain the front-end build: file list and compile-spec generation, IP and library collateral management, and automated quality checks on internal and third-party IP deliveries
* Build and maintain synthesis flows (Genus, Fusion Compiler, or Design Compiler): library and dont\_use setup, hierarchy strategy, clock gating, DFT hooks, and QoR reporting, with correlation to post-route results
* Build lint, CDC, and RDC infrastructure (SpyGlass, Jasper, Questa, or equivalent): rule sets, constraint and waiver methodology, and sign-off criteria. Tune them on real designs to separate real issues from noise
* Build formal equivalence flows (Conformal LEC or Formality) from RTL through netlist and ECO. Automate setup, mapping, and first-pass triage of non-equivalence and aborts, including low-power-aware LEC
* Develop RTL power-intent flows: UPF guidelines and checks for RTL owners, low-power static checks (VC LP / Conformal LP) at RTL and netlist, and consistency with the implementation UPF
* Build automated detection and reporting of common RTL and synthesis issues so designers catch them before handoff: unintended latches, logic optimized away, undriven or multi-driven nets, black boxes, and unexpected area or power
* Bring up early RTL-level power and area estimation (e.g., Joules, PowerArtist) so designers see PPA impact during development
* Pilot every flow on real blocks and reference designs. Do the deep technical analysis needed to validate results, and iterate with RTL and PD engineers until the flow is right

  
**What You'll Bring**

* Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent experience
* Typically 8+ years in front-end CAD, design methodology, synthesis, or RTL design for complex SoCs at advanced process nodes
* A track record of building front-end flows or tools that other engineers adopted and relied on through tapeout
* Deep technical understanding of the problems those flows solve, enough to build checks that are correct and to explain any result to a designer
* Hands-on experience running these flows on real designs and digging into the results: debugging constraint problems, synthesis QoR, and LEC failures yourself
* Hands-on experience with Genus, Fusion Compiler, or Design Compiler; Conformal LEC or Formality; and lint/CDC/RDC tools
* Working knowledge of UPF, low-power static checks, and how RTL power intent carries into implementation
* Strong Python and Tcl, plus software engineering habits: version control, testing, CI, and config-driven design that others can extend
* Ability to work independently on a small team: understand what designers need, take an ambiguous problem to a deployed solution, and explain technical trade-offs clearly to RTL and PD engineers

#### **Benefits**

Along with competitive pay, as a full-time Tesla employee, you are eligible for the following benefits at day 1 of hire:

* Medical plans > plan options with $0 payroll deduction
* Family-building, fertility, adoption and surrogacy benefits
* Dental (including orthodontic coverage) and vision plans, both have options with a $0 paycheck contribution

jobs.title: RESEARCH ASSISTANT III- Zwick Lab
jobs.description:
**ABOUT US:** Scripps Research is a nonprofit biomedical institute ranked as one of the most influential in the world for its impact on innovation. We celebrated our 100-year legacy in 2024. This significant milestone marks a century of seminal discoveries in immunology, infectious diseases (such as COVID-19, flu, HIV), neuroscience, heart disease, cancer, and more. Located in La Jolla, California, the institute houses six research departments, multiple Nobel laureates, a top-ranked graduate school and a leading postdoctoral training program. Scripps Research encompasses two elite and highly innovative institutes, the Calibr-Skaggs Institute for Innovative Medicines and Scripps Research Translational Institute, which merge foundational studies in biology, chemistry and computer science with translational science to produce pioneering drugs and advances in digital and precision medicine. Together, we cultivate new scientific leaders and expand the frontiers of knowledge to deliver medical breakthroughs impacting human health around the globe. If you have a passion for making a difference, this could be your opportunity to join our transformative team.

**POSITION TITLE:** Research Assistant III

**POSITION SUMMARY:**

The Zwick Laboratory in the Department of Immunology & Microbiology at Scripps Research is seeking a **motivated and highly organized Research Assistant (RA II or RA III, depending on experience)** to join our team studying antibody responses and developing next-generation vaccines and biologic therapies.

Our research focuses on **HIV vaccine design, broadly neutralizing antibodies, HIV envelope (Env), and germline-targeting immunogens**, with opportunities to extend these approaches to other viral pathogens and antibody-based therapies. Current studies combine molecular and cellular immunology, virology, antibody biology, flow cytometry, next-generation sequencing, and structure-guided vaccine design, including vaccine studies in mouse and nonhuman-primate models.

We are especially interested in someone who enjoys hands-on experimental work, wants to understand the scientific questions behind the experiments, and can grow into increasing responsibility within the laboratory.

In this position you will plan and conduct complex or novel research projects that involve the performance of non-routine procedures, development of new or improved techniques and evaluation criteria, thorough data analysis and complex interpretations of results; assist in designing experiments; operate sophisticated scientific lab equipment; may plan and conduct a small or average size project or a large portion of a more diverse project; may supervise or provide work direction and training to a small staff of professional-level employees; perform other related duties, tasks and responsibilities as required or assigned.

**RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES:**

The successful candidate will contribute directly to ongoing research and, depending on experience, may:

* Maintain, transfect, and characterize mammalian cell lines, including stable cell lines
* Perform flow cytometry and fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS), including data analysis and standardized presentation of results
* Carry out PCR and prepare samples for next-generation sequencing
* Perform ELISA and other antibody-binding and functional assays
* Support HIV virology and antibody neutralization studies
* Organize, analyze, interpret, and clearly present experimental data
* Coordinate experiments with laboratory personnel, Scripps core facilities, collaborators, and external service providers
* Maintain accurate experimental records, sample inventories, and laboratory workflows
* Troubleshoot experiments and communicate progress, problems, and next steps promptly
* As experience grows, assist with training junior personnel and day-to-day laboratory organization

Prior experience in either **immunology/cell biology or molecular biology/virology** would be valuable. Candidates do not need experience in every technique; we are looking for someone who is technically capable, eager to learn, and interested in developing breadth across these areas.

**REQUIREMENTS:**

* Bachelor's degree or higher in biology, immunology, microbiology, molecular biology, biochemistry, biotechnology, or a related field.
* Requires a minimum of 5 years’ experience.
* Candidates possessing a master’s degree, 3+ years’ experience required.
* Strong experimental organization and attention to detail
* Reliability, productivity, follow-through, and effective communication
* Ability to troubleshoot and manage several ongoing experimental priorities
* Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with others
* Interest in increasingly interpreting data and understanding how individual experiments contribute to the larger scientific question

We are especially interested in candidates looking for a **stable position with opportunities to grow in responsibility over time**. For the right person, the position offers the opportunity to take on increasing responsibility for experimental coordination, laboratory organization, mentoring, and day-to-day research operations.

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:**

This position works in a laboratory or vivarium environment. Further details of the physical requirements of established essential functions for this position will be addressed/discussed during the interview process.

**COMPENSATION:** The expected hiring range for this position is $72,384 - $84,375 per year, commensurate with experience. Consideration will be given to experience that exceeds the listed requirements.

**COMPREHENSIVE BENEFITS INCLUDE:**

* Employer Contributed Retirement Plan – Depending on eligibility, employees receive an employer contributed retirement plan (no employee contribution required) and the option to contribute to a 403(b) (which is similar to a 401(k) using your own pre or post-tax dollars)
* Full Suite of Health and Welfare plan

Our Microscopy and Histology Core supports researchers with FFPE tissue processing, sectioning, staining, and advanced multiplexed imaging. We’re looking for a Microscopy Specialist to join our small, collaborative team. You’ll be the hands behind the high-quality sections that feed into everything from routine histology analysis to spatial transcriptomics and multiplexed imaging projects.

* Process incoming samples and track them through our work order system
* Help investigators with sample preparation questions, such as fixation and trimming

The Tesla SI Hardware team is at the forefront of revolutionizing artificial intelligence through cutting-edge hardware innovation. Building these well takes real technical depth. You will bring each flow up on real blocks, analyze the results until you understand exactly why the tools report what they do, and turn that understanding into a system that gives designers correct, actionable answers. You are not the one fixing every CDC violation, but you understand them well enough to build the flow that helps every designer find and fix their own.

 **What You'll Do**

* Architect and build the RTL-to-PD handoff system: automated quality gates for elaboration, lint, CDC/RDC, SDC, UPF, smoke synthesis, and LEC. Give RTL and PD engineers clear pass/fail criteria they trust
* Build the timing constraint (SDC) flow: constraint linting, block-vs-top and RTL-vs-netlist consistency checks, and templates or generators for common clocking and I/O structures. Produce reports that point designers to the root cause instead of encouraging more exceptions
